note: Week 9 · one to play · Week 10 ahead
lede: Mark is three clear on twenty-two after watching his own 49ers put 38 on his own Raiders, which is the kind of week he is having. Behind him the table has never been tighter: half a point separates Jon and Bill in second and third, a single point covers Brian, Harrison and Patrick in fourth through sixth, and Week 10 draws both of those pairs against each other. Buffalo at Minnesota tonight closes Week 9 with Jon's twentieth point on the line, the trade deadline passes Tuesday afternoon, and on Sunday night Pittsburgh goes to Cincinnati with second place in this league attached to it.

beats.text: Jon against Harrison, the last game of Week 9, and both teams are 6-1. Minnesota is without Kyler Murray, who strained a hamstring and has been pointed toward a return next week, so Carson Wentz takes it against a Buffalo side with the highest-scoring offense in football at 33.3 a game. Josh Allen has eleven touchdown passes and nine more on the ground. A Buffalo win puts Jon on twenty and a point and a half clear of Bill; a Minnesota win lifts Harrison past Brian into fourth.

Jon at Bill, and the schedule could not have drawn it better. Both teams are 6-2, both have won four straight, they are tied at the top of the AFC North, and their owners are half a point apart in second and third. Pittsburgh won the first meeting 30-27 in Week 3 and holds the tiebreak. Joe Burrow has 23 touchdowns against six interceptions and has thrown three or more in four consecutive games; Aaron Rodgers has thirteen and six, with T.J. Watt on eight sacks. Cincinnati by three and a half.

beats.tag: Harrison and Patrick · Half a point, and they meet twice
beats.text: Sixteen and a half against sixteen, and two of the four games each man has are against the other. New England goes to Detroit in Munich at half past nine Sunday morning, where the Lions have won four in a row and Drake Maye is carrying eleven interceptions to Jared Goff's two. Then Houston at Cleveland, where the Texans lead the league with 29 sacks and the Browns have not named a quarterback since Shedeur Sanders started at New Orleans with Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol. Harrison also has Washington on Thursday and Minnesota at Green Bay.

beats.tag: Brian · Four games, and three of them are fights
beats.text: Seventeen points and fourth, with the busiest slate in the league outside the byes. Jacksonville is 6-2 and goes to Tennessee having won the last five in that series — that one is straight against Jon, as is Kansas City at Atlanta. New Orleans hosts Carolina against Patrick, two 3-5 teams tied at the bottom of the NFC South and the tightest line on the board. Seattle at Las Vegas is against Mark, with both quarterback rooms a question: Sam Darnold is a long shot on a quad and ribs and Drew Lock has an issue of his own.

beats.tag: Anthony · Two games, and the wrong two
beats.text: Both byes in the league this week are his, and they are the wrong halves of his roster. Denver sits at 7-2 on a five-game winning streak after a fifth fourth-quarter comeback of the season in Carolina, and Philadelphia sits too — which at least stops the bleeding at seven straight losses. That leaves him the Jets, 2-7 and beaten four in a row, hosting Buffalo; and Arizona, 3-6 and held to three points in Seattle, hosting a Rams side that has won three straight. He is on fourteen, and a quiet week here could be expensive.

beats.tag: Zach · Monday night, and still nothing from the Chargers
beats.text: Twelve points and last, and the problem is unchanged: Los Angeles is 0-8, the only winless team left, scoring 14.1 a game with Justin Herbert on ten interceptions, and they went twelve straight quarters without an offensive touchdown before Houston put 44 on them. They close Week 10 in Baltimore against Mark on Monday night, where the Ravens are 4-5, have lost four in a row and are starting Jacoby Brissett with Lamar Jackson on injured reserve. If the Chargers are ever going to win one, that is the spot.
